ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Static and cidal are not the same as target

A microbiology laboratory tests several protein synthesis inhibitors against susceptible bacteria. A trainee assumes that every drug in this broad group merely stops growth without killing. Which class is the most important commonly taught exception to that assumption?

  1. Lincosamides
  2. Chloramphenicol
  3. Aminoglycosides
  4. Tetracyclines
  5. Glycylcyclines
Answer and explanation

Aminoglycosides

Aminoglycosides are generally bactericidal despite acting on bacterial protein synthesis.

Option explanations

Aminoglycosides: Aminoglycosides are generally bactericidal despite acting on bacterial protein synthesis.

Tetracyclines: These are generally classified as bacteriostatic.

Glycylcyclines: These are generally classified as bacteriostatic.

Lincosamides: These are generally bacteriostatic; the standard broad-class exception is aminoglycosides.

Chloramphenicol: It is generally taught as bacteriostatic, although organism-specific exceptions exist.
